chapters.title: Chapter 5: Valuation in Indian Corporate Practice

lessons.title: Who Can Value a Company in India: Registered Valuers, Merchant Bankers and IBBI

children.text: A founder in Indore asks her chartered accountant for a valuation before issuing shares to a new investor. The report arrives, the round closes, everyone moves on. Eight months later the auditor asks for the registered valuer's report, and there isn't one. The number may have been perfectly sensible. It was signed by the wrong person for that particular purpose, and in India that is enough to cause a problem.

body.text: In Indian valuation, who signs the report is a legal question, not a matter of preference. Different laws name different professionals for different purposes, and a report from the wrong one is not a cheaper alternative. It is an invalid document.

children.text: Registered Valuers: The Companies Act Regime
Since October 2017, valuations required under the Companies Act, 2013 must be carried out by a
registered valuer

. Section 247 of the Act governs this, the Companies (Registered Valuers and Valuation) Rules, 2017 set out the machinery, and the Central Government delegated the role of authority to the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India.

markDefs.definition: A person or entity registered with the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India under the Companies (Registered Valuers and Valuation) Rules, 2017, for a specified asset class.

children.text: Three things are worth knowing about how somebody becomes one.
Registration is by asset class.
The three classes are securities or financial assets, land and building, and plant and machinery. A valuer registered for one cannot sign for another.
Membership of a registered valuers organisation is required.
These bodies enrol members, run training and handle discipline.
A valuation examination must be passed
, alongside the prescribed qualification and experience for that asset class.

cells: Securities or financial assets
Shares, debentures, business valuations, purchase price allocation
Members of ICAI, ICSI or the Institute of Cost Accountants of India, or an MBA with a finance specialisation, with the prescribed post-qualification experience
Land and building
Land, factory buildings, offices, real estate
Graduates and postgraduates in civil engineering, architecture or valuation of real estate, with the prescribed experience
Plant and machinery
Manufacturing equipment, vehicles, installed plant
Graduates and postgraduates in mechanical or electrical engineering, with the prescribed experience

body.text: The asset class mismatch is a real and common failure. A business valuation for a company whose main asset is a factory often needs two reports: a securities or financial assets valuer for the shares, and a land and building valuer for the property that sits inside that valuation. Check the registration number and the class on the report you are handed.

children.text: Merchant Bankers: Where Tax Law Insists
For several income tax purposes the law does not accept a registered valuer or a chartered accountant. It names a merchant banker registered with SEBI in Category I, and nobody else.

body.caption: Where a merchant banker is specifically required

cells: Fair market value of unlisted shares on the date an employee exercises ESOPs
The perquisite taxable in the employee's salary is computed from it
The report may be dated up to 180 days before the exercise date
Valuation supporting the price at which an unlisted company issues shares, under the income tax valuation rules
The rules prescribe who may apply the discounted cash flow and other methods
Under the amended Rule 11UA the report may be dated up to 90 days before the issue

children.text: The income tax valuation rules were widened in September 2023, adding five further methods for non-resident investors alongside discounted cash flow and net asset value: comparable company multiple, probability weighted expected return, option pricing, milestone analysis and replacement cost.

body.text: The so-called angel tax provision that made these valuations so fraught was abolished for all classes of investors from assessment year 2025-26. The valuation rules themselves did not disappear. They still govern other receipts of shares below fair market value, and they still sit alongside the separate FEMA pricing requirement, so the reports are still needed.

children.text: Chartered Accountants and Cost Accountants: The FEMA Route

When shares are issued to or transferred from a person outside India, the pricing is governed by the Non-Debt Instruments Rules made under FEMA. For an unlisted Indian company, the price must be worked out using an internationally accepted pricing methodology on an arm's length basis, certified by a chartered accountant, a SEBI registered Category I merchant banker, or a practising cost accountant.

body.label: Validity of a FEMA valuation certificate
body.context: If the allotment or transfer has not happened within 90 days of the certificate date, a fresh certificate is needed. This single line derails more Indian funding rounds than any disagreement about the valuation itself, because a round that slips a quarter quietly invalidates its own paperwork.

body.title: Has the certificate expired?
body.prompt: A FEMA valuation certificate is dated 15 June 2026. The company finally allots shares to its foreign investor on 20 September 2026. How many days have elapsed between the two dates?
body.explanation: 15 June to 20 September is 97 days: 15 remaining days in June, 31 in July, 31 in August and 20 in September. That is past the 90 day window, so a fresh certificate was required before the allotment. Diary the expiry date of every valuation certificate on the day you receive it.

children.text: One Table to Keep
This is the reference worth saving. The left column is what you are doing, the middle column is who must sign, and the right column is the rule that says so.

body.title: Who signs this one?
body.question: An unlisted Pune company is issuing fresh shares to a Singapore-based venture fund. Which valuation requirement applies to the pricing under exchange control law?
options: A registered valuer for land and building, because the company owns a factory
A chartered accountant, SEBI registered Category I merchant banker, or practising cost accountant, using an internationally accepted methodology on an arm's length basis
No valuation is needed, because the parties negotiated the price
body.explanation: This is a FEMA question, governed by the Non-Debt Instruments Rules, and those name the chartered accountant, Category I merchant banker or practising cost accountant. Note what the answer does not say: the same transaction may separately need a registered valuer's report under the Companies Act and a merchant banker's report for income tax purposes. One transaction can trigger three different requirements.

children.text: The Same Round, Three Reports

body.title: One quarter, how many valuations?
body.scenario: You are the finance head of an unlisted Bengaluru software company. In the same quarter the company plans to: issue fresh equity shares on a preferential basis to a Singapore venture fund, issue shares to two resident angel investors in the same round, and grant ESOPs to 30 employees, with an earlier group of employees exercising options granted three years ago. The founder asks why the auditors are talking about "four valuations" when there is only one company.
body.prompt: Explain what is required and why, and how you would sequence it.
body.modelAnswer:
What is required:
1. Companies Act. The preferential allotment needs a report from a registered valuer in the securities or financial assets class, supporting the price at which shares are issued.
2. FEMA. Issuing to the Singapore fund needs a certificate from a chartered accountant, Category I merchant banker or practising cost accountant, using an internationally accepted methodology on an arm's length basis. The issue price to the non-resident cannot be below that fair value, and the certificate is valid for 90 days.
3. Income tax. The share issue needs valuation support under the income tax valuation rules, where the prescribed methods must come from a merchant banker.
4. ESOP perquisite. When the earlier group exercises, the fair market value on the exercise date must come from a Category I merchant banker, and that is what drives the tax deducted from their salary. The fresh grant also needs a defensible exercise price.

Why it is not duplication: each report answers a different legal question, has a different prescribed signatory, and carries a different validity window. A single number that everyone accepts is convenient but not sufficient.

How I would sequence it:
5. Fix the target closing date first, then work backwards so that no certificate is more than 90 days old at allotment.
6. Appoint one merchant banker and one registered valuer early and share the same underlying financial model and assumptions with both, so the conclusions do not diverge without reason. Different purposes can justify different numbers, but unexplained differences invite questions from the auditor and the tax officer.
7. Handle the ESOP exercise valuation separately, because it is tied to the exercise date rather than to the round.
8. Keep a single file with each report, its date, its purpose, its signatory and its expiry. That file is what an auditor, a tax officer or a future acquirer will ask for.

children.text: What Makes a Report Stand Up

body.caption: The five things a reviewer checks first

cells: The signatory and registration number
Wrong professional for the purpose, or registered for a different asset class
The date and validity window
A certificate past 90 days, or an ESOP valuation dated after the exercise
The stated purpose
A report prepared for a bank loan reused for a share issue
The method and why it was chosen
Discounted cash flow used where the rules prescribe otherwise, or no reasoning given
Independence
A valuer who is also the company's statutory auditor or an interested party

body.text: A valuer must be independent of the company being valued. Do not ask your statutory auditor to sign the valuation for a transaction, and do not reuse a report prepared for one purpose in another. Both are cheap in the moment and expensive in a diligence review.

body.title: Two ways the same round is documented

columns.label: How trouble starts
points: One informal valuation note from a family CA, undated
Prepared for "the investors", with no stated purpose
Reused for the share issue, the ESOP grant and the tax filing
No registration number, asset class or method disclosed
Discovered two years later during due diligence for a larger round

columns.label: How it should look
points: Separate reports for each legal purpose, each naming that purpose
Signatory qualified for that purpose, with registration details on the face of the report
Valuation date, method, key assumptions and sources set out
Dates sequenced so no report expires before the transaction closes
All of it in one file, indexed by purpose and date

body.title: The authority
body.textWithBlank: Registered valuers in India are registered with the ___, which the Central Government specified as the authority under the Companies (Registered Valuers and Valuation) Rules, 2017.
correctAnswers: insolvency and bankruptcy board of india
body.explanation: The IBBI administers registration, the valuation examination and oversight of registered valuers organisations, in addition to its role under the insolvency code.

body.title: Before you accept a valuation report
steps: Confirm the purpose stated in the report matches what you need it for
Check the signatory is the professional the relevant law names for that purpose
For a registered valuer, check the registration number and that the asset class fits
Note the valuation date and the expiry window, and diary the expiry
Confirm the method used is permitted for that purpose, and that the reasoning is stated
Look for the key assumptions: growth, margins, discount rate, and any discounts applied
Check independence: no conflict with the auditor, the promoters or the counterparty
File the report with its purpose and date, and keep the underlying model

body.label: IBBI: registered valuers and valuer organisations
body.description: Search for a valuer by name or registration number and confirm the asset class they are registered for. Do this before appointing anyone, not after the report arrives.

cards.definition: Registered with the IBBI under the 2017 rules for a specific asset class. Required for most Companies Act valuations.
Securities or financial assets, land and building, or plant and machinery. Registration is class-specific.
The professional body a registered valuer must belong to, which handles enrolment, training and discipline.
A SEBI registered merchant banker, named specifically in income tax valuation rules for unlisted shares and ESOP perquisites.
The Non-Debt Instruments Rules under FEMA, which govern pricing when shares are issued to or transferred from non-residents.
The window within which a FEMA valuation certificate, and a report under the amended income tax rules, must be used.
The provision of the Companies Act, 2013 that requires valuations under that Act to be done by a registered valuer.

points: In India the signatory is part of the legal requirement. A sound number signed by the wrong professional is not a valid valuation for that purpose.

Registered valuers are registered with the IBBI under Section 247 of the Companies Act, 2013 and the 2017 rules, by asset class: securities or financial assets, land and building, or plant and machinery.
Income tax rules name a SEBI registered Category I merchant banker for unlisted share issues and for ESOP perquisite fair market value.

FEMA pricing for unlisted shares can be certified by a chartered accountant, a Category I merchant banker or a practising cost accountant, using an internationally accepted methodology, valid for 90 days.
One funding round can trigger three or four separate valuation requirements, each with its own signatory and validity window.
The angel tax provision was abolished from assessment year 2025-26, but the valuation rules and the FEMA requirement continue.
Check purpose, signatory, asset class, date and independence before accepting any report.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and is not legal, tax or investment advice. Requirements are summarised in outline, change frequently through amendments and notifications, and depend on the facts of each transaction. Confirm the current position and the applicable signatory with a qualified professional before relying on any valuation report.
